c.tagline: Cobblestones, Art Nouveau spires, and Baltic charm on the Daugava.

taxi.fareNote: Use licensed taxis (Red Cab, Panda Taxi) or book via Bolt app to avoid tourist overcharging at Old Town taxi stands.

emergency.note: 112 is the universal EU emergency number and reaches all services; English-speaking operators are generally available.

avoid.reason: Pickpocketing in the Old Town; stag-party nightlife scams — rip-off bars and taxis

hood_desc: Riga's cobblestoned medieval core packed with Gothic spires, cafes and the Freedom Monument, ideal for first-time visitors who want everything within walking distance.
Leafy boulevards lined with Europe's finest Art Nouveau facades and upscale boutiques, suited to architecture lovers and travelers wanting an elegant, quieter base close to downtown.

A leafy left-bank residential district with wooden houses, a historic covered market and a growing cafe scene, good for travelers wanting a local, less touristy feel with easy tram access to the center.
A bohemian strip of independent cafes, craft breweries and street art in the Avoti area, popular with younger travelers and creatives seeking Riga's hipster side.
The gritty, up-and-coming zone around the Zeppelin-hangar Central Market and train station, offering cheap eats and budget stays within walking distance of Old Town.
lodging: Riga Old Town Hostel & Backpackers Pub

water.note: Meets EU standards and is safe to drink; even ice in bars and restaurants is made from treated tap water.

transit.pay: Buy single tickets, day passes, or top up an e-talon smart card at kiosks, ticket machines, or the Rīgas satiksme app; contactless bank cards can now also be tapped directly on trams and buses. Tickets bought from the driver cost more than pre-purchased ones.
transit.hours: Most routes operate roughly 5:30am-11:30pm; a few night bus/tram lines run later on weekends.
transit.note: Validate or tap your ticket immediately after boarding; fare inspectors issue on-the-spot fines for invalid tickets.

train: Latvian Railways (Vivi) domestic and regional trains
International rail-bus combinations to Vilnius and Tallinn (Rail Baltica under construction)
bus: Rīgas satiksme city buses, trolleybuses and trams
Ecolines and Lux Express intercity/international coaches
ferry: Stena Line overnight ferry to Stockholm

tip.r: Not obligatory; rounding up the bill or leaving 5-10% in restaurants for good service is customary and appreciated.
